title: SaaS & MVP development
short: Turn an idea into a launch-ready product, then keep improving it with real users.
intro: We scope, design, build and deploy your first version, then iterate with real usage so the product grows in the right direction.

audience.title: Non-technical founders
audience.text: You know the problem and the customer. We bring the product thinking and the engineering team.

audience.title: Businesses productising a tool
audience.text: You built something internally that others would pay for and want to turn it into SaaS.

audience.title: Teams rebuilding a product
audience.text: Your first version proved demand but the code cannot carry the next stage.

audience.title: Agencies with a product client
audience.text: Your client needs a real product, not a website, and you need a reliable build partner.

problems.problem: Unclear scope and a feature list that keeps growing
problems.fix: A discovery sprint that ranks features and fixes the smallest version worth launching

problems.problem: A slow, expensive path to the first paying users
problems.fix: A fixed-scope first release, with weekly progress you can see and test

problems.problem: Fragile code that breaks as soon as users arrive
problems.fix: A clean architecture, code reviews and automated deployment from day one

problems.problem: No plan for billing, user roles or analytics
problems.fix: Subscriptions, roles, permissions and product analytics built into the first release

features.title: Accounts and onboarding
features.text: Sign-up, login, social sign-in, team invites and a first-run experience that gets users to value quickly.

features.title: Subscriptions and billing
features.text: Plans, trials, invoices and payment providers such as Stripe, set up so you can change pricing later.

features.title: Roles and permissions
features.text: Owners, admins and members with the right access, ready for multi-tenant SaaS.

features.title: Admin panel
features.text: A back office for your team to manage users, content, plans and support requests.

features.title: Analytics and events
features.text: Product events and dashboards so you can see what users actually do.

features.title: Integrations and APIs
features.text: Email, notifications, third-party tools and a documented API if your customers need one.

steps.title: Discovery sprint
steps.text: We map users, the core workflow and the smallest version worth launching.
steps.output: Written scope, feature priorities and timeline

steps.title: Product design
steps.text: User flows, wireframes and a clickable UI you can test before code is written.
steps.output: Approved designs and a clickable prototype

steps.title: Build in sprints
steps.text: Features shipped to a test environment in short cycles with weekly updates.
steps.output: Working software you can review every week

steps.title: Launch
steps.text: Production setup, domain, SSL, payments, monitoring and store or web release.
steps.output: A live product and a launch checklist

steps.title: Iterate
steps.text: We read real usage and feedback, then plan and build the next improvements.
steps.output: A prioritised roadmap for the next release

faqs.q: How long does an MVP take?
faqs.a: Most MVPs take 6–12 weeks. You receive a written timeline after the discovery sprint.

faqs.q: Will I own the code?
faqs.a: Yes. You own the code, designs and accounts, with a full handover.

faqs.q: Can you help decide what to build first?
faqs.a: Yes. Discovery is where we prioritise the smallest version that proves value.

faqs.q: I am not technical. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: No. We explain decisions in plain language and recommend the technology, so you can focus on customers.

faqs.q: What happens after launch?
faqs.a: You can keep us on a care plan or a monthly team to fix issues, ship improvements and scale the product.

faqs.q: Can you take over an existing MVP?
faqs.a: Yes. We start with a code and infrastructure review, then recommend whether to improve or rebuild parts of it.

steps.title: Use-case workshop
steps.text: We map repetitive tasks and decisions, and pick the ones where AI agents or automation clearly save time.
steps.output: Ranked use cases with effort and risk

steps.title: Proof of concept
steps.text: A small working agent, assistant or workflow tested on your real data.
steps.output: A demo and a go or no-go recommendation

steps.title: Build and integrate
steps.text: Production build inside your product or tools, with tool access, guardrails and approvals.
steps.output: AI agents and workflows live in your operations

steps.title: Evaluate and review
steps.text: Test sets, accuracy checks, edge cases and human review steps.
steps.output: Evaluation results and review process

steps.title: Monitor and improve
steps.text: Usage, quality and cost tracking, with prompt, retrieval and workflow tuning over time.
steps.output: A dashboard and regular improvements

faqs.q: What is an AI agent, in plain terms?
faqs.a: Software that uses an LLM to decide what to do next and then does it with your tools, such as searching records, updating a CRM or sending a follow-up, within limits you set.

faqs.q: What is RAG and why does it matter?
faqs.a: Retrieval-augmented generation means the AI looks up answers in your own documents and data before replying, so answers are specific to your business and easier to check.

faqs.q: Is our data safe?
faqs.a: We use providers that do not train on your data, limit access, and keep sensitive data out of prompts where possible. Self-hosted open-source models are an option too.

faqs.q: Can AI work inside our existing system?
faqs.a: Yes. We integrate agents and AI features into your current product, CRM, helpdesk or internal tools.

faqs.q: How do you keep answers and actions accurate?
faqs.a: We ground answers in your content, evaluate them against test cases, add guardrails, and keep a human approval step for important actions.

faqs.q: What will it cost to run?
faqs.a: AI providers charge per use. We estimate running costs during the proof of concept and add spend limits.

faqs.q: Can the assistant work on WhatsApp?
faqs.a: Yes. We can connect assistants and agents to your website, WhatsApp Business, email or internal tools.

faqs.q: Where should we start?
faqs.a: With one repetitive task that costs your team time every week. A small win first makes the next step clearer.
